title: Security doodles + open questions for SOC2 runbook
content:
Purpose: quick messy brain-dump of control ideas, evidence locations, and open questions while we iterate the SOC2 runbook. Not polished — intended to be ephemeral notes I can convert later.

Topline: we need a compact mapping from our infra/app artifacts to SOC2 criteria (Security primarily, Availability secondary). Below are sketched control owners, candidate evidence, and the gaps I saw when walking through infra yesterday.

1) High-level control clusters (sketch):
- Identity & Access Management (IAM): console + infra + service accounts lifecycle
  - owner idea: infra-sre (Elias) + eng-security
  - candidate evidence: IAM policy export (GCP IAM JSON), service-account key rotation log (KMS), onboarding/offboarding checklist PRs in HR ops folder
  - quick note: need a short runbook for 'revoke key on offboard' that non-SREs can trigger (pager playbook link?)

- Change Management / Deployment Controls:
  - owner idea: release-engineering
  - candidate evidence: GitLab MR approvals, CI job artifacts (signed build metadata), deployment runbook history, canary rollout config for model-serving routes
  - gap: how do we capture approvals for emergency bypasses? suggestion: tag MR with EMERGENCY-BYPASS and attach incident ticket id.

- Logging & Monitoring / Alerting:
  - owner idea: observability
  - candidate evidence: centralized logging index (logstash/elasticsearch index names), alert routing policies (PagerDuty policies), SLO dashboards (console)
  - gap: retention windows vary across datasets — need authoritative retention table and an evidence artifact showing configured retention per index

- Data Protection / Confidentiality:
  - owner idea: trust-ops + product-security
  - candidate evidence: KMS key rotation schedule, storage ACL snapshots, dataset access control list export, redaction scripts for dev logs
  - gap: dev/staging datasets sometimes mirror prod — do we have a strict mask/obfuscation policy documented? if not, quick mitigation: enforce deny-by-default in staging projects and rotate keys used for any real PII above X sensitivity.

2) Rough control mapping (plain text table)
Control ID | TSC area | Owner | Candidate evidence 
C-01 IAM-Lifecycle | Security | infra-sre | gcp-iam-export-2026-02.json, offboard-checklist.md
C-02 Deploy-Approval | Processing integrity | release-eng | MR-approvals, pipeline-artifacts.zip
C-03 Logging-Retention | Availability/Security | observability | logs-index-retention.csv, alert-policy-v2.yaml

(These IDs are placeholders — will map to the canonical SOC2 control numbers once we sync with auditor template.)

3) Evidence inventory (quick bullet list)
- Identities: GCP IAM export (projects: redwood-prod, redwood-staging) — file path: /infra/iam-exports/2026-02-10.json
- Secrets: KMS config + last rotation audit (kms-rotation-2026-01.pdf) — stored in vault-evidence bucket, access: security-team-only
- Deployments: gitlab MRs with required approvers (group: release-approvers) — query: label:needs-approval AND merged_at:>2025-12-01
- Backups: nightly backup manifest for databases (s3://backups/db-manifest-2026-02.csv)
- Access reviews: last quarterly access review deck (Q4-2025-access-review.pptx) — note: overdue for Q1-2026

4) Observed gaps & risk notes (quick):
- Access review cadence slipped — last reviewer list incomplete. Consequence: stale service accounts with broad privileges. Remediation: automate monthly list and email owners (low friction)
- Some ephemeral infra (ad-hoc GCP projects for experiments) are not captured under central billing/org policies — risk: shadow resources. Short-term: tag sweep script + add to infra-onboarding checklist
- Evidence fragmentation: docs live in Confluence, Gitlab, S3, and local drives. Need canonical index (single source of truth) and cross-links in runbook.

5) Questions for auditor / TODO items to clarify before formal mapping:
- Auditor asks for 'authorization proof' for change control: is MR approval + release pipeline logs sufficient, or do we need a signed change request? (Action: ask during scoping call)
- How granular do they want retention evidence? per-index config or single retention policy doc?
- For on-prem customers (private deployments), do we include their audit copies as separate evidence bundles? probably optional but document process.

6) Tactical action list (1–2 week sprint)
- Build 'evidence index' doc (spreadsheet) and link to canonical artifacts — owner: me (Jasper) — due: 2026-03-12
- Add runbook snippet for offboard + key revocation (playbook template) — owner: Elias — due: 2026-03-08
- Run a one-off access-review sweep and produce a snapshot (CSV) for auditor — owner: Maya — due: 2026-03-10
- Create a temporary 'emergency-approval' MR label workflow and document usage — owner: release-eng — due: 2026-03-05 (prototype)

7) Random scribbles/doodles I drew while thinking (verbalized):
- Diagram: central control plane (console) -> dedicated infra (reserved GPUs) -> private customers (VPC) — need mapping of where logs flow for each boundary (hosted vs private)
- Quick policy idea: enforce 'no-long-lived-keys' by policy — any service account key older than 30 days flagged and auto-rotated unless an exception PR exists (exception tracking could be a tiny spreadsheet to start)

8) Notes-to-self / followups:
- Sync with Maya re: quarterly access review backlog — ask for export of last 18 months of changes
- Call with auditor scheduled: 2026-03-09 11:00 PT — prepare list of 10 'must-have' evidence items and 5 'nice-to-have' items
- Convert this doc to structured runbook pages once gaps are resolved.

End — messy but usable. If collaborators want to add inline notes, scribble below.

---- inline scratch area (temporary) ----
- Idea: a tiny script `evidence-checker` that verifies existence of all artifacts in the index (checks S3, Confluence permalinks, GitLab MR lists) — MVP could be a shell script + python glue.
- Risk prioritization: mark any gap that affects customer-facing endpoints (auth, encryption, availability) as P0. Everything else P1/P2.

(temporary signature) Jasper L. — will clean and export to Confluence after 2026-03-12 sprint completes.
